check: how a user would enable wall generation on a real machine
answer: There is no user-facing way. The current jar cannot generate a wall in a normal world, by design.
whatEnablingRequires: -Dgreatwall.s1c.productionFixture=true as a JVM argument, which an ordinary player cannot set
greatwall.production left unset, since setting it throws 'Formal production remains OFF until S1C acceptance'
a file named greatwall_s1c_fixture in the game directory
a file named greatwall_test_world in the game directory, separately required by WorldServices:96
noConfigFile: src/main/resources contains only fabric.mod.json and the mixins config. The only configDir references in the codebase read other mods' files - tectonic.json and c2me.toml - for the generation fingerprint, not to configure this mod.
commandsAreDiagnostics: The greatwall command tree is status, stats, reset-session, locate, plan, job status, job cancel, verify segment/range/loaded and rebuild. All query or repair; none enables generation.
interpretation: This is consistent with everything else recorded: the acceptance entries all say production OFF, and the fixture conditions describe an isolated laboratory world rather than a player feature. The preview is not a playable release, and the honest statement of that is that installing it changes nothing.
whatThisMeansForTheUser: Any expectation of walking a generated wall on the real machine requires the S1C acceptance path to be opened first. That is a scope question, not a bug.
